methodological_rigor.justification: The in vitro design has significant gaps: no positive drug control (e.g., doxorubicin, tamoxifen) was included in any cell-based assay despite being used as reference in docking; no IC50 values were calculated to permit quantitative potency comparison; and no power calculation or justification for n=3 triplicates is given. There are internal inconsistencies between text and figure captions regarding concentrations (e.g., wound healing described at 10/20 μg/mL in the body but 15/30 μg/mL in captions; clonogenic assay captioned at 10/20 μg/mL but reported in text at 15/30 μg/mL), which undermines confidence in reporting fidelity. The docking validation reports identical RMSD and binding energy (0.70 Å, −14.41 kcal mol−1) for both hERα and PI3Kα targets — an implausible coincidence that is not reconciled. Statistical analysis is limited to ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc without multiplicity correction across multiple compounds/concentrations/timepoints, no effect sizes or confidence intervals are reported, and no handling of outliers or missing data is addressed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro cytotoxicity study on two breast cancer cell lines combined with in silico docking and ADME prediction, which maps to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is modest: the compound is a plant-derived triterpenoid saponin with only cell-line evidence at μg/mL concentrations, no mechanistic confirmation of the predicted hERα/PI3Kα targets, and no selectivity data against non-cancerous cells. The ADME prediction itself indicates poor oral bioavailability (score 0.17, low GI absorption, multiple Lipinski/Ghose/Veber/Egan/Muegge violations plus a BRENK alert) for TM36, which further limits its translational path toward clinical development without substantial medicinal chemistry optimization.

reporting_quality.justification: No formal animal work was performed (cell lines only), so no checklist maps perfectly; ARRIVE is the closest preclinical standard but adherence is partial — randomization/blinding of scoring in colony counts and wound-healing image analysis is not described, nor is passage number, mycoplasma testing, authentication of cell lines, or seeding uniformity across replicates. Methods for extraction/characterization are off-loaded to a prior publication without recapitulation; concentrations and sample sizes conflict between text and captions; and no raw data, image set, or docking input/output files are referenced. There is no explicit data or code availability statement in the manuscript, and no repository identifiers (e.g., for docking poses, NMR spectra, or image analysis scripts) are given beyond supplementary tables.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is an incremental empirical contribution: it screens five previously characterized oleanane-type triterpenoids/saponins (terminolic acid, arjungenin, arjunglucoside I, 24-deoxysericoside, chebuloside II) from Terminalia macroptera against two standard breast cancer cell lines, with routine SwissADME and AutoDock analysis. The compounds themselves are not newly isolated — the authors explicitly reference prior isolation/characterization work (ref 24) — and oleanane saponins have been widely studied for antiproliferative activity against MCF-7/MDA-MB-231. The modest novelty is the specific application of 24-deoxysericoside to breast cancer cytotoxicity assays, but no new mechanism, no new scaffold, and no first-in-class claim is substantiated; discussion acknowledges the mechanism of related saponins is already well established.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable but contains repeated grammatical slips (e.g., 'from stable complexes of relative binding energies', 'treated as well as untreated ones at a density', 'at after 48 h', 'reference [REDACTED]' broken citations) and awkward constructions throughout. Section organization is adequate but the Discussion is largely a rehash of general background on triterpenoid/saponin anticancer activity rather than specific interpretation of the data. Caption/text inconsistency on concentrations (10/20 vs 15/30 μg/mL in colony and migration experiments) is a major clarity problem that would confuse any reader attempting replication, and the Discussion references a solvent 'E8' in the Methods wound-healing paragraph with no definition.

key_strengths: Clear ethnobotanical motivation and a reasonable screening panel of five structurally related oleanane triterpenoids/saponins from a single medicinal plant
Integration of in vitro cytotoxicity with molecular docking against two mechanistically relevant breast cancer targets (hERα and PI3Kα) plus SwissADME profiling
Explicit identification of 24-deoxysericoside as the lead compound with concentration-dependent effects in MTT, clonogenic, and wound-healing assays
key_concerns: No positive drug control in any cell-based assay and no IC50 values calculated, preventing quantitative potency benchmarking against standard chemotherapeutics

Internal numerical inconsistencies between text and figure captions for concentrations in colony-formation and migration assays (10/20 vs 15/30 μg/mL), plus an identical docking-validation RMSD/binding-energy pair reported for two distinct targets
Statistical analysis lacks effect sizes, confidence intervals, multiplicity correction, and any power/sample-size justification; only n=3 triplicates
ADME predictions themselves show poor drug-likeness for the lead compound (bioavailability score 0.17, multiple rule violations, BRENK alert) which contradicts the manuscript's optimistic framing
Novelty is incremental — compounds are previously isolated and the saponin/triterpenoid class is well-studied against MCF-7/MDA-MB-231; no mechanistic validation of docking predictions is performed
No formal data or code availability statement; cell-line authentication, mycoplasma testing, passage number, and blinding of image/colony counts are not reported
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent but highly incremental preclinical phytochemistry/cell-line screening paper with notable rigor gaps (no positive control, no IC50, inconsistent concentrations, no multiplicity correction) and modest novelty, placing it at Tier 4 (specialty natural-products/phytochemistry journals) with major revisions needed to reconcile internal inconsistencies and strengthen methodological reporting.
